name: Pommard

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.

notes: Pommard is among the most powerful and tannic reds of the Côte de Beaune.
It contrasts with the light, elegant wines of neighboring Volnay.

blurb.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy making red wine only, mainly from Pinot Noir. It has no Grand Cru vineyards but several highly regarded Premier Crus, and the AOC dates from 1936.
